response.text:
Recent work supports decomposing recommendation feedback into explicit judgments rather than one helpfulness score. [ALERT (NAACL 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.137.pdf) uses pairwise explanation preferences, structured subquestions and annotation guidelines; reported Krippendorff’s α=0.24 highlights substantial disagreement. A [2025 HCI+NLP paper](https://aclanthology.org/anthology-files/pdf/hcinlp/2025.hcinlp-1.20.pdf) recommends collecting evidence or reasoning alongside labels, piloting instructions, and preserving meaningful disagreements. Practical adaptation: attach an exact feedback span and identified item to every diagnostic label; independently double-code feedback and report raw agreement plus chance-corrected agreement before adjudication.

For this task, a proposed taxonomy—not an established taxonomy verified by these sources—is: immediate choice; explicitly deferred relevance; explicit incompatibility; explicit duplication; lower-ranked alternative preferred to a higher-ranked item; unidentified-item/insufficient-evidence abstention. Keep temporal relevance separate from rejection, and record pairwise preferences only when the comparison is explicit. Ground item properties in public titles/descriptions and user claims in quoted feedback; ownership, specifications and mood remain unknown unless stated. Report counts with eligible denominators, including deferred-choice frequency, explicit preference reversals and abstention reasons.

Selective prediction research emphasizes balancing errors against coverage: [ReCoVERR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15610) demonstrates that additional evidence can reduce unnecessary abstention in visual question answering. Its application here is methodological: report annotation coverage together with audited error among accepted labels; never interpret abstention as dislike. Twenty training users support descriptive diagnosis and hypothesis generation, not validation-performance or population-level claims. Model selection remains the fixed macro validation HR@10.
